A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCALE research work. All 22 pages in each version, including Appendices A–L, equations, eight figures, and fourteen tables, support reliable comparison after text extraction and visual inspection.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulation and real-world robot experiments in Tables 1–5, component ablations, qualitative examples, and additional empirical analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original simulation and real-world results, ablations, qualitative examples, and appendix analyses. These include the work’s own SCALE evaluations, alongside results attributed to prior methods.

M1.justification: The dual-reference uncertainty measure, adaptive action sampling, EMA-based visual attention modulation, Algorithm 1, and backbone-specific procedures remain unchanged. Appendix J corrects an equation reference without changing the described procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LIBERO suites, SIMPLER-WidowX tasks, LIBERO-PRO-Long perturbations, and three in-distribution plus two out-of-distribution real-world tasks. Training data coverage is also retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain greedy decoding, temperature sampling, top-k, top-p, RoboMonkey, TACO, and MG-Select. The uncertainty-metric comparators in Table 7 and Two-step Oracle in Table 9 are unchanged; Self-Certainty only receives capitalization edits.

E3.justification: The fine-tuned and zero-shot settings, success-rate metric, episode counts, preprocessing, training budgets, and hyperparameter-selection procedures remain the same in Section 4.1 and Appendices F–L. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the component and visual-modulation ablations, uncertainty-metric comparison, previous-step versus oracle analysis, latency measurements, qualitative cases, and baseline/SCALE sensitivity analyses. Their tested questions and supporting evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report simulation results over three seeds and provide the same means and standard deviations in Appendix K, Table 12. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, SCALE’s LIBERO averages remain 81.5% with OpenVLA and 93.0% with pi0-FAST; the oracle, per-task, and sensitivity results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, KL-difference derivation in Appendix B, posterior interpretation and equal-prior assumption in Appendix C, and baseline-metric formulas in Appendix J are retained. The equation-reference correction changes no mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: uncertainty-conditioned joint adaptation of perception and action, no additional training or verifier, single-pass inference, and improved performance over VLA and TTS baselines.

C2.justification: The interpretations of component synergy, temporal uncertainty, and visual grounding remain unchanged. Both retain Appendix A’s distinction between conviction and correctness and Appendix L’s explanation of failures from excessively broad visual attention.

D1.justification: Appendix J corrects the implementation reference for replacing the sigmoid with normalized baseline metrics from Equation 2 to Equation 4, the temperature-scaling equation. This improves documentation accuracy; hardware, hyperparameters, training instructions, and code-access information are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds an extra Jang et al. (2025) citation to its overview of test-time action sampling and verification. This is a limited attribution addition: MG-Select was already discussed in v2, and the bibliography and substantive research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 replaces many em dashes with commas, colons, or connecting words, makes small grammatical edits, standardizes Self-Certainty capitalization, and removes redundant wording in Appendix I. The section order and narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 and Table 8 receive caption punctuation edits, while Tables 6–7 receive small header or label edits. Text reflow changes some column and page breaks, but all figures and tables retain their designs, content, and numbering.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves documentation accuracy and consistency, particularly by directing Appendix J’s implementation instruction to the correct temperature-scaling equation. Naming and language cleanup provide additional limited benefits. The method, empirical support, theory, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is small.
